checks.description: Interleaved LFENCE/RDTSC latencies for leaves 0,1,7,0x40000000,0x40000100,0x80000000; compares largest and smallest medians. Research heuristic also triggered by real CPU leaf-cost differences; not VMAware CPUID_SIGNATURE.

fix.how: Calibrate on comparable bare metal and minimize exits and host scheduling noise. TSC offsetting/scaling and exit-cost compensation require coordinated hypervisor work; a static offset cannot remove per-exit cost and clock compensation must remain consistent across vCPUs and clocks.
fix.chimera: Not fixable by configuration. cpuidmon -s rewrites CPUID values but turns every CPUID into a vm_event round trip to dom0 (about 35x the plain exit cost, see the G2 numbers); masking through the Xen CPUID policy instead (xl.cfg cpuid=, verify that Xen 4.19 honours clearing the bit for HVM) removes the monitor cost but not the ~2.5k-cycle exit. Hiding the exit itself needs Xen-side TSC compensation for CPUID exits, which Xen 4.19 does not have; tsc_mode, TSC scaling and vCPU pinning do not remove per-exit cost. CHIMERA G2 measurements (2026-10-29, i7-13700HX host): median RDTSC;CPUID;RDTSC 2398-3720 cycles on the Xen HVM guest without an introspection monitor and 92530-94514 cycles with DRAKVUF cpuidmon -s, which forwards every CPUID to the dom0 monitor; al-khaser's avg10 rule fired 1000/1000 in every configuration, dom0 included (1590-1964 cycles).

checks.description: Research side channel. Batched (8 calls per clock read) latency of a failing call that registry/file monitors trace (Windows: NtOpenKey on a random absent key; Linux: openat of a random absent name in /), of a cheap syscall (NtQueryInformationProcess / getpid) and of a user-mode arithmetic reference. Detected when a median exceeds the traced floor or the traced call is far slower than the cheap one. Moderate confidence; cannot name a monitor.

fix.how: Trace fewer calls, or only the calls an analysis needs; each traced call costs a trap. Keep in-guest filter drivers and audit rules to what the image needs.
fix.chimera: Every DRAKVUF breakpoint trap (syscalls, regmon, filetracer, procmon plugins) is a VM exit plus a vm_event round trip to dom0, which costs tens of microseconds per call. Disable plugins that are not needed for a run, and prefer the syscalls plugin's filter (-S) to tracing every system call. The cost cannot be hidden from the guest.

checks.reason: Unsafe: the EIP_OVERFLOW probe can crash Xen guests. Never executed, even under deep profile.

fix.how: Do not run this destabilizing probe. Use safe guarded instruction and timing observations and review the hypervisor separately.
fix.chimera: Excluded because Xen guest stability is a binding requirement. A process-level signal/exception guard cannot recover a guest/kernel crash.

checks.description: Reads the code of a small compiled function (entry to RET) for INT3 encodings (0xCC, CD 03) without executing it. Hidden EPT/altp2m breakpoints read as the original bytes.

fix.how: Do not set software breakpoints in the sample from inside the guest; use hardware or hypervisor breakpoints.
fix.chimera: DRAKVUF breakpoints are hidden through altp2m shadow views, so they read as original bytes; a detection here means an in-guest debugger patched the code.

checks.description: NtQueryObject(ObjectTypesInformation): the DebugObject type's object/handle count is nonzero while any user-mode debugging session exists in the guest.

fix.how: Do not attach a user-mode debugger to the sample or to other processes in the analysis guest; launch samples normally and observe from outside the guest.
fix.chimera: DRAKVUF is agentless and attaches no Windows debugger, so this should be clean on CHIMERA. A detection means a debugger or troubleshooting tool was left in the golden image or the launcher.

checks.description: SeDebugPrivilege enabled in the own token, or csrss.exe (CsrGetProcessId) openable for PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION. al-khaser CanOpenCsrss asks for PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS; query access keeps the probe read-only. Elevated administrative launchers can also enable the privilege.

fix.how: Launch the sample with a normal user or filtered admin token; do not enable SeDebugPrivilege for it.
fix.chimera: Check the CHIMERA launcher: a sample started from an elevated service context with SeDebugPrivilege enabled looks debugged.
